options.summary: Move Status Complete (or success acknowledgement) downstream so it only runs after final clean/repair-clean branch is confirmed and preferably after send-prep knows outcome.
pros: Strong sequencing guarantee against premature success
Keeps success UX for clean path
cons: Connection reorder risk: Status Complete is currently a sequencing bridge into Restore → Close Lock → Parse Mode → Send
May require duplicate status nodes or extra connections
Higher risk to lock/memory chain than in-place wording gate
options.verdict: defer_as_secondary — only if Option D field gating fails in sandbox

options.summary: Replace success preface with neutral processing text for all paths (e.g. «Задача обработана. Проверяю итоговые материалы…»).
cons: On reject path, neutral «проверяю материалы» can still mislead if materials are already blocked
options.verdict: partial — absorb only if D cannot read outcome fields safely

options.summary: Suppress success preface entirely; let final materials or reject diagnostic be the first final-status operator message (Status Final progress may remain).
pros: Node delta 0 if Status Complete becomes no-op / honest progress / skipped edit
cons: Clean path loses early «готово» acknowledgement before materials
Must not break sequencing if Status Complete is required as connection bridge
options.verdict: fallback — preferred if D gating proves unsafe

options.summary: Split final status messages by outcome while keeping Status Complete position: clean/repair-clean → success wording; blocked-dirty/reject → blocked/reject wording only; errors → error wording only.
pros: Outcome already known at Status Complete (after Format* / Take First)
Format Strict Reject already emits memory_status=blocked_dirty and blocked_diagnostic
Node delta 0 expected (expression-only on Status Complete text)
cons: Must define reliable field predicates for clean vs reject vs error
Must keep HTML parse_mode safe for status edits
Must not alter HOTFIX02 reject send path

rationale: Committed topology shows Status Complete already runs after Format* where outcome fields exist, and before lock/send. Outcome-gated wording at the same node (Option D) fixes false success without rewiring the lock/send bridge. Option C remains the minimal fallback.
